newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast electricity again holds steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast electricity again holds steady.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity values in the southeastern U.S. again held steady Wednesday in thin discussion, industry sources said.
"We saw pretty much a carbon copy of yesterday," said one southeastern power marketer.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Thursday was said to be holding at $21.00-$23.50 a megawatt hour.
Firm, off-peak electricity for next-day delivery was said to be less expensive at $14.00-15.00 from $15.00-$16.00 discussion on Tuesday.
In the northern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) system, firm, peak electricity was assessed steady from Tuesday at $17.00-$18.00, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak, firm power in northern TVA for Tuesday delivery was mostly pegged unchanged near $12.00.
TVA did not offer its own generation for next-day sale for a third day in a row, according to market sources.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
